{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary estimand intercurrent event strategy incomplete",
      "quote": "Start of new anti-cancer therapy prior to PFS event",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary estimand lists 'Start of new anti-cancer therapy prior to PFS event' as an intercurrent event but does not specify the strategy (e.g., treatment policy, while on treatment) for handling it. The description only says PFS is censored, which is a composite strategy, but the strategy type is not explicitly named.",
      "fix": "Explicitly state the intercurrent event strategy (e.g., 'treatment policy' or 'while on treatment') for start of new anti-cancer therapy in the estimand attributes."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of PFS censoring",
      "quote": "PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 3.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary estimand description says PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy, but the endpoint definition says PFS is time until progression or death, whichever occurs first. Censoring at start of new therapy is a strategy, but the description is ambiguous about whether events after new therapy are ignored or censored. This could lead to inconsistent analysis.",
      "fix": "Clarify that PFS events occurring after start of new anti-cancer therapy are censored at the last evaluable assessment before that start, and specify the strategy in the estimand."
    },
    {
      "title": "Crossover criteria inconsistent with early efficacy statement",
      "quote": "Alternatively, should an early efficacy of the study be noted by the DMC, crossover will be considered for all subjects who randomized into the docetaxel arm",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 4.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The design states crossover is offered after radiological progression, but also says crossover will be considered for all subjects if early efficacy is noted by DMC. This is a potential inconsistency: if crossover is allowed before progression, it may affect the OS estimand that assumes 'regardless of crossover' but the timing of crossover could introduce bias.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether early crossover is allowed before progression and how it will be handled in the statistical analysis, especially for OS and PFS."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing definition of 'early efficacy'",
      "quote": "should an early efficacy of the study be noted by the DMC",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 4.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions 'early efficacy' but does not define what constitutes early efficacy or the criteria for DMC to recommend crossover. This is a critical missing detail that could lead to operational ambiguity and potential protocol amendments.",
      "fix": "Define the criteria for early efficacy (e.g., interim analysis results) and the process for DMC recommendation and implementation of crossover."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent tumor assessment schedule",
      "quote": "every 6 weeks from cycle 1 day 1; (± 7 days) (at weeks 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, 37, 43, and 49), and then at 9 week intervals (± 7 days) thereafter",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 4.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The schedule says every 6 weeks but lists weeks 7, 13, 19, etc., which are 6-week intervals from week 7 (i.e., 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, 37, 43, 49). However, the first assessment is at week 7, not week 6, which is inconsistent with 'every 6 weeks from cycle 1 day 1'. This could cause confusion in scheduling.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the first tumor assessment is at week 6 or week 7, and align the text accordingly."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing details on treatment beyond progression",
      "quote": "See Section 8.1.6 and Section 8.1.7 for AMG 510 and docetaxel treatment beyond radiologic progression.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 4.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The synopsis references sections 8.1.6 and 8.1.7 for treatment beyond progression, but these sections are not provided in the text. The protocol body is missing these details, which are important for understanding the trial design and participant burden.",
      "fix": "Include the referenced sections in the protocol body or provide a summary of the rules for treatment beyond progression."
    },
    {
      "title": "Incomplete secondary estimand for PRO",
      "quote": "PRO measurements before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy including crossover will be used to estimate treatment effect.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The PRO estimand does not specify the handling of missing data or the strategy for intercurrent events other than start of new therapy (e.g., treatment discontinuation due to toxicity). This could lead to ambiguity in the analysis.",
      "fix": "Specify the intercurrent event strategies for PRO endpoints, including handling of missing data and discontinuation."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of disease control rate",
      "quote": "Disease control rate - defined as rate of confirmed objective response (CR or PR) + stable disease per RECIST v1.1 of at least 6 weeks measured",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "M11 3.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The DCR definition says 'stable disease per RECIST v1.1 of at least 6 weeks measured' but does not specify whether stable disease must be confirmed or how it is measured. Also, the phrase 'measured' is awkward and unclear.",
      "fix": "Clarify the DCR definition, e.g., 'stable disease for at least 6 weeks as assessed by BICR' and specify whether confirmation is required."
    }
  ]
}
